title: Crossing the Rhône
summary: Cross the Rhône by one of several prepared routes, sever the eastern supply road, and capture two Roman advance camps before Scipio reaches the river.
teaching_goal: A camp is taken by standing in it, not by levelling it. Nine men cannot kill thirty-eight, but they can hold two gate yards long enough to claim them - and a Roman column without its commander stops being a column.
narrative_intent: A broad river operation with ferries, wooded detours, bridgeheads, and fortified supply quarters; the Iron Sepulcher occupies an avoidable ruin on the southern flank.
historical_context: 218 BC: Hannibal crossed the Rhône upstream from its mouth using boats, rafts, and a detached force sent across to turn local opposition. Scipio arrived too late; this altered history places Roman advance camps on the far-bank road to create the opening Carthage-versus-Rome engagement.

victory_conditions.description: Seize the two river forts. Leave no crossing for Scipio's army to inherit.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Cross before the Roman runners reach their garrison. Every second spent waiting feeds the blade.

stages.title: Reach the Rhone crossing
stages.description: Bring the column to the pontoon bridge on the near bank.
stages.hint: The river runs north to south across the middle of the valley; the nearest crossing is due east of camp.

stages.title: Seize the Roman hill fort
stages.description: Stand in the gate yard of the northern advance camp until it falls to Carthage.
stages.hint: A camp is taken by holding its yard, not by levelling it.

stages.title: Seize the river town
stages.description: Take the second camp on the southern supply road.
stages.hint: Scipio inherits any crossing you leave behind.

stages.title: Kill the Roman commanders
stages.description: A column without its commander stops being a column.
stages.hint: Enemy camps fall neutral once their commander is dead.

actions.text: Navigate through the maze of hills and valleys. Watch for enemy patrols!
Two bridges cross the Rhône. Choose your path wisely - you may need both routes!
The Roman villages are heavily defended. Coordinate your attacks!

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: So. The Barcid crawls down to the Rhone. Cross where you like - the river is not particular about whose bones it keeps, and Rome has a great deal of patience and a very great many shovels. My surveyors are already pacing out your grave. They tell me the ground here drinks well.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: You have the river town. My congratulations - you now own three hundred mouths, two wells, and a temple whose god has lately been asking after Carthage by name. Feed them. I shall come back in the spring and count what is left.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: You killed a consul. Good. Rome keeps forty more in cupboards in the city, and I promise you the ones still in the cupboards are worse. He will be missed - briefly, and only by his creditors.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Take the crossings, then. Take the whole cold length of the road north and every stone laid on it. Rome does not lose provinces - she lends them, at interest, and I am told the collectors on this road wear no faces at all.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: There. Sit down in the mud with the others. They tell me the men who die on this road do not stay where they are put - that they rise about the third watch and go on marching north without their officers. Do continue. You are expected.

theme: The river is wide, the far bank is guarded, and every minute standing still costs blood.
